text:
For **excoriation (skin-picking) disorder**, look for a therapist or psychologist who specifically treats **BFRBs**—body-focused repetitive behaviors—and uses **ComB (Comprehensive Behavioral Model), habit-reversal training, CBT, ACT, or ERP**.

### Texas providers offering online care

- **Angela Malek, M.Ed., LPC** — Telehealth-only across Texas; treats skin picking and hair pulling using **ComB, CBT, behavior therapy, and ERP**. Works with teens and adults; lists UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Scott & White, and Lyra among accepted plans. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/angela-malek?utm_source=openai))
- **Suzanne Mouton-Odum, Ph.D.** — Houston-based psychologist offering telehealth to Texas clients; specializes in BFRBs, OCD, and anxiety, and treats children, teens, and adults. Uses CBT, ComB, habit-reversal training, ACT, and related approaches. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/suzanne-mouton-odum%2C-ph.d.?utm_source=openai))
- **Michele Rose** — Telehealth provider licensed in Texas; treats skin picking with ComB, habit-reversal training, CBT, ACT, and mindfulness. Works with children, teens, and adults; primarily private pay or out-of-network benefits. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/michele-rose?utm_source=openai))
- **Aaron Edmiston, LPC / Blueprint Therapy Services** — Offers secure telehealth throughout Texas when clinically appropriate; treats excoriation disorder and other BFRBs, including children, teens, and adults. ([blueprinttherapyservices.com](https://www.blueprinttherapyservices.com/hair-pulling-skin-picking-treatment?utm_source=openai))
- **Donald A. Schroeder, LPC** — Offers online treatment for skin picking and hair pulling, with CBT, ComB, and habit-reversal training; lists some insurance plans and sliding-scale availability. ([psychologytoday.com](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/therapists/texas-hair-pulling-trichotillomania-skin-picking-spring-tx/1037416?utm_source=openai))
- **Priscilla Elliott, LPC** — Leads an online adult BFRB group via Google Meet, including skin-picking disorder. The group is listed at **$50 per week**, with an initial interview required. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/treatment_group/bfrb-group-for-adult-skin-pickers-hair-pullers-and-nail-biters/?utm_source=openai))

### Best place to search

The **TLC Foundation for Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors** maintains a specialist directory and identifies providers by state, telehealth availability, age group, and BFRB specialty. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-and-therapeutic-providers?utm_source=openai))

### What to ask during a consultation

Ask:

1. “How many clients with **excoriation/skin-picking disorder** do you treat?”
2. “Are you trained in **ComB or habit-reversal training**?”
3. “Do you offer **telehealth to clients physically located in Texas**?”
4. “Do you accept my insurance, or provide superbills?”
5. “Can you coordinate with a dermatologist or psychiatrist if needed?”

If you want medication evaluation, look for a **psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner** in addition to a BFRB-focused therapist. If picking has caused spreading redness, warmth, pus, severe pain, fever, or deep wounds, see a medical clinician promptly. Availability, fees, and insurance participation can change, so confirm those details directly.
